Privacy Policy

A plain-language overview of how this website handles information.

Information you choose to share

The project enquiry form asks for your name, business email, company, country, service interest and project requirements. Budget and timeline are optional. When the secure form is configured, these details are stored in LetsFygure's Supabase database so the team can respond. The form does not report success unless the database confirms the save.

Service providers

Supabase provides form data storage. Resend may process the same enquiry details to notify the LetsFygure team by email. If you choose the separate WhatsApp action after submitting, WhatsApp processes that message under its own terms. Browser credentials for Supabase and Resend are not exposed by the form.

Technical and security information

Hosting infrastructure may process standard request information needed to deliver and protect the website, such as IP address, browser type and request time. A one-way representation of the IP address may be used temporarily for rate limiting. No analytics product is currently described or implied here.

Retention and your choices

Do not include passwords, payment card details, identity documents or confidential third-party material in an initial enquiry. Contact LetsFygure at the email address on the contact page to ask about access, correction or deletion. A final production retention schedule must be approved by LetsFygure before launch.

External links

Links to Clutch, Instagram, client websites and WhatsApp take you to third-party services whose privacy practices are governed by their own policies.

Start with a bounded decision

Good first use cases have a recognizable input, a useful output and a person who already owns the decision. Classification, extraction and drafting often fit better than open-ended autonomy.

Prioritize the content and assets needed for the first useful view. Font strategy, responsive images and server rendering often matter more than cosmetic loading animation.

Large client bundles and unnecessary third-party scripts compete with the user. Keep the browser's main thread available for navigation, forms and meaningful feedback.

The most useful technical decisions begin with the operating reality: the people doing the work, the information they trust and the constraints the product cannot ignore.

01
Start with a bounded decision

Good first use cases have a recognizable input, a useful output and a person who already owns the decision. Classification, extraction and drafting often fit better than open-ended autonomy.

02
Design the exception path

Confidence thresholds, source context and human approval are product features. They make uncertain output visible and give the workflow somewhere safe to go when automation should stop.

03
Measure usefulness, not novelty

Create a representative test set and review accuracy, time saved, corrections and failure modes before expanding the workflow.

Working principle

Prefer a smaller system with explicit boundaries and observable behavior over a larger promise that cannot be tested.
